name: Afghanistan
people: Where Afghans at home and abroad, and their friends, design the nation they want to live in.
codesigner: Everyone who shares a vision, a voice or an enterprise here becomes a Co-designer of Perfect Afghanistan: one of a community of selfless people, at home and abroad, building a nation where every citizen has a decent life. You may take part under a pen name.

paras: Your mountains have stood over the crossroads of Asia for thousands of years. … Picture Perfect Afghanistan: every daughter walks to school beside her brother, the snowmelt of the Hindu Kush is stored and shared, and no Afghan falls below a decent life, because the nation has decided that none will.
letter.quote: “A nation is not its government. This Letter is written to the farmer, the nurse and the child, and to every daughter who wants to finish school.”

mandates.terms: For Afghanistan’s development partners, humanitarian agencies and investors, and for Afghans at home and abroad. Scope and fees are agreed in writing before any work begins.

capita.pc_text: The yearly cost, per person, of lifting everyone above the Living Line in all seven basic living standards, set with Afghanistan in its own prices.
capita.price_text: Perfect Capita times the population: the national bill, each year.
capita.est: Perfect Nations estimate, from the latest published figures. Shelter has no national measure and education is barred by decree, so neither is scored.
capita.measures: Strict measures. Food: share not in acute food crisis (IPC Phase 3 or above), the worst season of the year; 19.2 million people were projected in crisis in the winter of 2026–27. Water: safely managed drinking water. Shelter: no national measure of housing quality exists, so none is given. Energy: electricity used per person (5,850 GWh in 2022, divided by the World Bank population), against 1,000 kWh; about four-fifths of it is imported. Education: barred by decree for girls after grade six and for women at university; learning poverty from a 2022 analysis. Health: WHO service coverage index; the bar on women’s medical training is reported by the United Nations. Livelihood: share above the national poverty line. Each figure links to its source.

unscored.heading: Perfect Capita cannot be reached while any citizen is barred by law.
unscored.text: No score is given while girls are barred from school after grade six and women from university. Of the standards that are measured, energy is lowest, at 14.
unscored.definition: The poverty line measures income. The Living Line measures a life: food, water, shelter, energy, education, health and livelihood. Perfect Capita is the yearly cost, per person, of lifting everyone above the Living Line in all seven basic living standards. Coverage scores each standard strictly out of 100, and a nation is held at its weakest. In Afghanistan, girls are barred from school after grade six and women from university, so no score is given. Of the standards that are measured, energy is lowest, at 14, then water at 31.

voices.local: We are looking for the people with real stories from Afghanistan: the teachers, farmers, health workers and builders who keep things working, at home and in the diaspora. Guests may speak under a pen name, and with their voice changed.

close_lead: Share your vision, suggest a guest, or write to us. Every message receives a personal reply, and a pen name is always welcome.
